property.text: RLP-encoded account data received from P2P peers MUST be validated against size constraints before parsing. Malformed RLP data MUST NOT cause excessive memory allocation, crashes, or panics.

reachability.notes: Malicious P2P peer can send crafted RLP data designed to trigger excessive memory allocation or parser bugs.

property.severity_justification: Malformed RLP causing excessive memory allocation or crash is a DoS vulnerability exploitable by any P2P peer.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating node crash or excessive resource consumption via crafted RLP data.

property.text: A block containing a large number of deposit events MUST NOT cause excessive CPU usage that degrades block processing performance beyond acceptable bounds. The per-event validation cost in extract_deposit_data MUST be bounded.

reachability.notes: Gas limits bound the number of deposit events per block, but if per-event validation cost is disproportionately high, this could still be exploitable. Out-of-scope if it requires sustained high-effort attack.

property.severity_justification: CPU-intensive block processing could cause temporary node slowdown but is bounded by gas limits.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Likely out-of-scope as a high-effort single-peer DoS attack requiring on-chain transactions. Only in-scope if single packet/transaction causes disproportionate CPU usage.

property.text: If a deposit event at DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS has malformed data that fails extract_deposit_data validation, the entire block MUST be rejected (InvalidBlock). The deposit contract being a system contract does not exempt it from data validation.

reachability.notes: If the deposit contract can be called in a way that produces malformed events (e.g., via a bug in the contract or unexpected calldata), blocks containing such events must be rejected.

property.severity_justification: If an attacker can reliably trigger malformed deposit events, they can force rejection of all blocks containing deposit activity, disrupting validator deposits.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating attacker-triggered malformed deposit event causing block rejection.

property.text: The Uint.from_be_bytes parsing of offset values in extract_deposit_data MUST NOT be susceptible to integer overflow. In implementation languages with fixed-width integers (Go, Rust, Java), the parsed offset value MUST be bounds-checked before comparison.

reachability.notes: The Python spec uses arbitrary-precision Uint, but Go/Rust/Java implementations use fixed-width integers. A crafted offset value near max(uint64) could overflow and bypass validation.

property.severity_justification: Integer overflow in offset parsing could bypass validation, allowing extraction from wrong positions. In memory-unsafe languages, this could cause buffer overflows.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating integer overflow in offset parsing in a specific EL implementation (Go, Rust, Java).

property.text: The Engine API communication of requests hash from EL to CL MUST be authenticated via JWT. Unauthenticated Engine API calls MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: Engine API authentication is infrastructure-level. Vulnerabilities requiring exposed Engine API are out-of-scope per contest rules.

property.severity_justification: Unauthenticated Engine API access would allow injection of incorrect requests hashes, causing the CL to finalize incorrect state.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Out-of-scope per contest rules: vulnerabilities requiring publicly exposed API.

property.text: The requests hash computation in compute_requests_hash MUST be deterministic. forall (requests_list): given the same input list, compute_requests_hash MUST always return the same SHA-256 digest.

reachability.notes: Non-deterministic hash computation would cause intermittent consensus failures, which would be extremely difficult to diagnose and could cause random network splits.

property.severity_justification: Non-deterministic hash computation would cause intermittent, hard-to-diagnose consensus failures affecting the entire network.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Internal implementation correctness issue. Critical but not externally triggered.

property.text: Buffer reads in extract_deposit_data MUST NOT access memory beyond the bounds of the input data. forall (data_slice in extract_deposit_data): start_index >= 0 AND end_index <= len(data).

reachability.notes: In memory-unsafe languages, incorrect bounds on data slicing could read beyond the buffer, leaking adjacent memory contents or causing crashes.

property.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds read could leak sensitive memory contents or crash the node, depending on implementation language.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating out-of-bounds read in extract_deposit_data in a specific EL implementation.

property.text: The keccak256 hash function used in encode_account MUST be collision-resistant. forall (code1, code2): code1 != code2 => keccak256(code1) != keccak256(code2) (with overwhelming probability).

reachability.notes: keccak256 provides 256-bit security. Practical collisions are computationally infeasible with current technology.

property.severity_justification: Theoretical concern only. A keccak256 collision would break the fundamental cryptographic assumption of the entire Ethereum protocol, not just this module.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Finding a keccak256 collision would be a breakthrough in cryptography, far beyond this specific audit scope.

property.text: The deposit_requests accumulator MUST be initialized to empty bytes (b'') at the start of parse_deposit_requests. No residual data from previous calls may be present.

reachability.notes: Internal initialization requirement. Failure would only occur due to implementation bug in buffer management.

property.severity_justification: Residual data in the accumulator would corrupt deposit requests and cause requests hash mismatch.

property.text: The receipt decoding in parse_deposit_requests via decode_receipt MUST be compatible across all EL implementations. forall (receipt_bytes): decode_receipt(receipt_bytes) MUST produce identical log lists across all EL clients.

reachability.notes: Different receipt decoding across implementations would produce different log lists, leading to different deposit sequences and consensus divergence.

property.severity_justification: Receipt decoding inconsistency would cause deterministic consensus divergence between EL clients.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating different decode_receipt outputs across two EL implementations for the same receipt bytes.
